content.rendered:
Therefore take no thought, saying, What shall we eat? or, What shall we drink? or, Wherewithal shall we be clothed? 32  (For after all these things do the Gentiles seek:) for your heavenly Father knoweth that ye have need of all these things.33 But seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you.

MATTHEW 6:31-33 KJV

The idea that there is a kingdom of God that we are to seek as the verse above commands implies that there are other kingdoms and indeed there are. The bible speaks of the Kingdoms of this world which can also be called the Kingdom of men. There is also the Kingdom of Darkness which is ruled by Satan and his princes (principalities) as Ephesians 6:12 and Colossians 1:13 say. Daniel 4:17 shows that while God sets the basest or the lowest of men on these thrones as He wills, there is a realm above these for those called the Holy watchers, who have the right and ability to influence the Kingdoms of men. These watchers are those, like the prophet Jeremiah who plants kings and remove Kings, Jeremiah 1:9-10. These holy ones are also those who war against the kingdom of darkness that influences the Kingdoms of men. Hence, in Revelation 11:15, when the final battle is won, there was a cry saying “The kingdoms of this world has become the Kingdom of our God and His Christ and He shall reign forever”.

This is the Kingdom we are to seek, the Kingdom of our God. Jesus mentioned that we are not to move like the gentiles move. One who is a child of God must seek to understand, enter and inherit the Kingdom of God. Yesterday, we read from John 3:3-5 that being born again simply gives us the right to see the Kingdom of God. For one to enter the Kingdom of God, they need to be born of water and of the Spirit. This is because there is an awareness that the Spirit of God gives a believer, when they are born again, that there is another realm of life. The moment you are born again, the Spirit of God comes into you, as Paul says, whoever does not have the Spirit does not belong to Christ, Romans 8:9. However, we need to go beyond seeing to living by the Word and by the leading of the Spirit. We are to work out our salvation with fear and trembling as Philippians 2:12 says.

Jesus also mentioned that for one to enter the Kingdom, they need to repent and be like a little child, Matthew 18:3. This is the result of working out our salvation. Like a child, offences do not mesmerize and this individual who has a change of mind to become like a child will live above a lot of nuances that affect christians today. Jesus also mentioned that our righteousness must be greater than the scribes and pharisees, who live hypocritically and preach but do not live by the Word of God, Luke 11:39-48. In Matthew 7:21, Jesus warned that “Not everyone who says to Me, ‘Lord, Lord,’ shall enter the kingdom of heaven, but he who does the will of My Father in heaven“. It is not enough to be born again. Being renewed by the washing of the water of regeneration via the Word of God and the regeneration of the Holy Spirit as we follow His lead is what gives us the ability to enter the Kingdom of God, Titus 3:5, Ephesians 5:26. That is, living by the Word of God and following the lead of the Spirit is what enables us enter the Kingdom of God.

In Luke 22:29-30, Jesus said “And I bestow upon you a kingdom, just as My Father bestowed one upon Me, [30] that you may eat and drink at My table in My kingdom, and sit on thrones judging the twelve tribes of Israel.” It is the Father’s good pleasure, not only to show us the Kingdom, but that we may enter and inherit the Kingdom of God. The charge to us is that we do not just have faith and leave it fallow, we are to labour to enter into this Kingdom . As James 2:16-26 says, by works, faith is made perfect. Not the work of the flesh, but the work of faith which is obedience to God’s word. Beloved, the Kingdom set before us is great and the promise is great, labour to enter and inherit the Kingdom. Let this be your chief quest and Joy. It has been given unto you. 

Prayer for today: Heavenly Father, thank you for bestowing on me a Kingdom that will never fail or be overthrown by any other. It is your pleasure to give me this Kingdom. Father help me to diligently live by Your Word and follow Your Spirit, that I may not only see the Kingdom, but I may  enter and inherit this Kingdom as a Son of God. I pray in Jesus name. Amen.

content.rendered:
Therefore take no thought, saying, What shall we eat? or, What shall we drink? or, Wherewithal shall we be clothed? 32  (For after all these things do the Gentiles seek:) for your heavenly Father knoweth that ye have need of all these things.33 But seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you.

Matthew 6:31-33

Jesus’ entire ministry for three an a half years was centred around the gospel of the Kingdom of God. The Kingdom of God is the dominion of God, God as the king over visible and invisible things. Psalm 24:13 says God is the King of glory. Therefore Christ, when asked when the Kingdom is coming, said that the Kingdom is within man, Christ in you, the hope of glory, Luke 17:20-21, Colossians 1:27. Man in connection with God at the beginning was given the dominion to express the Kingdom of God on earth, Genesis 1:26-28, but when he chose to define good and evil and fell, he lost all dominion to the devil. This is what Jesus came to restore to man.

What is the Kingdom of God? It is a person, Jesus Christ in us. Matthew 6:33 says “But seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you”. This means by priority, the Kingdom of God must be manifested in your lifestyle. Doing things in the right way is living is righteousness. Therefore, sometimes, the bible would call a person who was not a Jew, righteous, Acts 10:22. There is a right way, a kingdom way to do everything including prayer, giving, living every day life, leisure, marriage, etc. The Kingdom of God is also not meat and drink or material things, as the Jews mistook it to mean, Romans 14:17. It is the power of the Holy Spirit operating in a person to bring righteousness, peace and Joy in the Holy spirit. If a person is struggling with any of these, they have most likely deviated from the path of the Kingdom.

How does one enter the Kingdom? Jesus answered and said unto him, Verily, verily, I say unto thee, Except a man be born again, he cannot see the kingdom of God. [4] Nicodemus saith unto him, How can a man be born when he is old? can he enter the second time into his mother’s womb, and be born? [5] Jesus answered, Verily, verily, I say unto thee, Except a man be born of water and of the Spirit, he cannot enter into the kingdom of God, John 3:3-5. The primary purpose for the coming of Jesus was not that we will be born again. Being born again only allows you to see the Kingdom. A man who is born again and does not grow only sees the Kingdom. The primary purpose Jesus came was to show us the way to the Father, John 14:6. Being born again gives you the exclusive right to see the Kingdom of God. However, you need to progressively move from being born again, to be being born of water and of the Spirit to enter the Kingdom of God.

We will explore the meaning of this phrase in a subsequent meditation. As Paul said, if a man does not have the Spirit of God in Him, he does not belong to the Lord. If we therefore have this Kingdom within us, we must live by its precepts. It is our responsibility to seek the Kingdom way in everything we do. This is what it means to seek first the Kingdom. Rather than doing things the way the of the Kingdoms of this world, seek first the Kingdom and His righteousness, that is the Kingdom way characterized by righteousness, peace and Joy and everything else will be added unto you. 

Prayer for today: My Father, King of heaven, Hallowed be your name. Lord, may your Kingdom and dominion be seen in my life and Your will prevail. Father, teach me how to live in the Kingdom way and not the way of the World. I receive the diligence to seek first the Kingdom of God and His righteousness, knowing that everything else will be added unto me. I pray in Jesus name. Amen.

content.rendered:
And he said unto them, I must preach the kingdom of God to other cities also: for therefore am I sent.

Luke 4:43 KJV

The Kingdom of God is a concept that seems simple, but it is one of the most misunderstood concepts. Jesus preached the gospel of the Kingdom to the Jews for three years, but they could not understand it. This was because they needed to repent. John the Baptist came as a voice crying in the wilderness with the message “Repent for the Kingdom of God is at hand”, Matthew 3:1-3. Repentance here involved having a change of heart so they could understand how the Kingdom actually comes. Many missed the coming of the Kingdom to earth, except a few like Anna and Simeon who had been praying for the salvation of Israel, Luke 2:25-39.

In Acts 1:1-8, after three years and forty days, His disciples still didn’t understand the message of the Kingdom. According to Acts 1:6-8, When they therefore were come together, they asked of him, saying, Lord, wilt thou at this time restore again the kingdom to Israel? [7] And he said unto them, It is not for you to know the times or the seasons, which the Father hath put in his own power. [8] But ye shall receive power, after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you: and ye shall be witnesses unto me both in Jerusalem, and in all Judæa, and in Samaria, and unto the uttermost part of the earth. The way they would learn about the Kingdom was when they had been endued with power from the Holy Spirit.

The two individuals who understood this mystery during Jesus’ ministry ironically were strangers. One was a centurion who understood what it meant to be a man under authority, being a man under the authority of Rome, Matthew 8:5-13. The other was the thief on the cross. While Jesus’ disciples were all scattered and the supposed King was hanging on the cross and being mocked by religious leaders. Yet this man got insight into the mystery of the Kingdom and by faith secured his spot in it, Luke 23:41-43.

What is the Kingdom? It is the dominion of God. In Genesis 1:26-28, God gave all the dominion on earth to man, but man lost it to the devil. Satan, while tempting Jesus in Luke 4:5 offered him the Kingdoms of the world. These weren’t high buildings and sky scrapers. Satan showed Him man. The kingdom of this world are men or that which is supposed to be expressed in man. Satan was offering Jesus the dominion over man to regain that which Adam lost to the devil because he chose the ability to define good and evil over the tree of life. Genesis 3:22 shows how the enemy came through the back door and lied to man, offering him immortality in a death sentence. Yet Jesus came to restore the dominion and eternal life to man.

In subsequent meditations, we will understand in more details what the Kingdom is and how enter it. The Kingdoms of this world will by necessity become the Kingdom of our God and of His Christ, Revelations 11:15. It is of necessity that we repent (have a change of heart) in order to appreciate the coming Kingdom and secure our lot in it.

Prayer for today: High King of Heaven thank You for coming down to us to pave the way for the coming Kingdom and to make the path clear for us to partake of this Kingdom. Father, I pray that the eyes of my understanding may be open to comprehend and appreciate the good news of the coming Kingdom and also be a partaker of it in Jesus name. Amen

title.rendered: 193 – If any man will be my disciple IV

content.rendered:
Then said Jesus unto his disciples, If any man will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross, and follow me. [25] For whosoever will save his life shall lose it: and whosoever will lose his life for my sake shall find it.

Matthew 16:24-25

Jesus lived in total obedience to His Father and exemplified that man can live in the same way. He said to His disciples “If a man love me, he will keep my words: and my Father will love him, and we will come unto him, and make our abode with him. [24] He that loveth me not keepeth not my sayings: and the word which ye hear is not mine, but the Father’s which sent me.” John 14:23-24. A proof of our love and devotion to God is that we live in total obedience as He did. Yesterday, we said that the practice of obedience is essential to all who are disciples because this is the mark of sons. We also mentioned that the heart beat of the Lord Jesus is for His Church. This should be the chief joy of all who will be disciples.

Sharing in labours of love is a key to our consecration as disciples. 1 Corinthians 12:6-7 says there are diversities of operations, but it is the same God which worketh all in all. [7] But the manifestation of the Spirit is given to every man to profit withal. A disciple is sharing in the labours of love when he identifies the gift God put within him and uses it to God’s standards with love and a heart of service. This service however is done from a place of friendship with the bridegroom, Jesus Christ, John 3:29-30. From this angle, the disciple will not be concerned with the praise and rebuke of men, because he seeks to please His friend and Lord only.

Often times, like in the case of Jesus, those who are being served may not appreciate it. They may even the ones to persecute. In the case of Jesus, those who He served tirelessly cried out “Crucify Him”. This brings us to another key. Being a disciple of Jesus therefore also means we have the same loving disposition to persecution that He did. Jesus never decided to stop His labours of Love because people reviled Him. Paul was settling a dispute in the Corinthian church where one of the saints defrauded another and it resulted in a court case. You would think Paul would rebuke the offender or validate the offended. Instead he said in 1 Corinthians 6:7 “Now therefore there is utterly a fault among you, because ye go to law one with another. Why do ye not rather take wrong? why do ye not rather suffer yourselves to be defrauded?” In our culture where people fear being doormats, this may not be readily acceptable, but it is the Word of God nonetheless.

Being a disciple of Jesus is no easy task, but it is possible and most rewarding. We are to take up our cross and die on it daily. Paul encourages us to examine ourselves, 1 Corinthians 13:5. He said in 1 Corinthians 11:31, For if we would judge ourselves, we should not be judged. It is good to have self examination on how we are fairing in the light of what we have learned of Jesus by observing Him. This is the last key to note. If we sit down daily before the judgement seat of the Holy Spirit and let Him tell us how we are fairing, we can be sure He would point out areas still needing work, but we will also appreciate the growth we have experienced by observing Him and living as He did. The beauty of being a disciple is that where He is, we will be also, John 14:1-4. Not as servants but as friends, because He gives us a unique insight into all that He does. This honour is exclusive to friends of God.

Prayer for today: Lord Jesus, I appreciate You. Thank you for not living us in the dark of what man should be. You came and lived out what man in the image of God looks like. Jesus help me to love like you loved, even those who revile and offend me. Give me Your kind of love that is patient and kind and does not keep record of wrong. The kind of love that will turn the left cheek and not leave the post of service because of an offense. Lord examine me, I already know I fall short in many areas, lead me in the path of life, for You are my God in Jesus name. Amen.

title.rendered: 192 – If any man would be my disciple III

content.rendered:
Then said Jesus unto his disciples, If any man will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross, and follow me. [25] For whosoever will save his life shall lose it: and whosoever will lose his life for my sake shall find it.

Matthew 16:24-25

Jesus came to earth as the pattern Son, to show us God’s intent for who man should be. Hebrews 2:10-11 says “Hebrews 2:10-11 “For it became him, for whom are all things, and by whom are all things, in bringing many sons unto glory, to make the captain of their salvation perfect through sufferings. [11] For both he that sanctifieth and they who are sanctified are all of one: for which cause he is not ashamed to call them brethren“. He came as the only begotten to raise more Sons who would be exactly as He is. So, He lived among men and lived as a man should be. Yesterday, we mentioned that the disciple observes the discipline of the one He follows and does as He sees. 

Jesus preached and taught His disciples to do so. He prayed and showed them that the way to succeed in all that God had given to them was to pray always. Hence, He said “Man ought always to pray and not to faint., Luke 18:1” Jesus was a diligent student of the Word and said “Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every Word that proceeds from the mouth of God”, Matthew 4:4. The next key Jesus showed them and which would characterize his disciples is being a doer of the Word. Jesus said to them, “My food is to do the will of Him who sent Me and to accomplish His work”, John 4:34. Jesus did only the will of His father, to the point that He said “I can of my own self do nothing”, John 5:30. Jesus came to show us that a true Son of the Father is one who is obedient and that the end of our faith is perfecting obedience to God, such that we can do absolutely nothing except what God wills. In essence, our rebellious soul is completely conquered and we are locked into God’s will.

So the practice of obedience is essential to all who are disciples because this is the mark of sons. Obedience to His Word is a proof that we love Him, John 14:15, and that we want to attain to that glory that He has promised us. He also gives us the ability to do all that He asks by His indwelling Spirit in us, Philippians 4:13. Another key Jesus showed us is how to be a servant of God and by extension, a servant of all men for God’s sake. Jesus said “The Son of man came not to be served, but to serve and to give His life as a ransom for many”, Matthew 20:28. Our appreciation of the Love of Jesus Christ to us, is to pledge our lives to His service and as we see in 2 Corinthians 5:14-15. If we say we love the Lord, we are called unto a life of service to Him.

What God wants each individual to do is different and He has put in man all He needs to accomplish the work. God’s heart beat is for His bride, His church, that she may be built up and prepared for His coming. As true disciples, our heart beat must be for the house of God as well. David bound himself to a oath regarding the house of God, saying “If I forget you, Jerusalem, may my right hand forget its skill.”Psalm 137:5. We are Jerusalem from above, Galatians 4:26, the Church of the first born and Mount Zion, as Hebrews 12:22-23 says. All who make Jerusalem their Chief Joy show their true devotion to God. The word of the Lord says “they shall prosper who love her”. 

Prayer for today: Lord Jesus, I want to be Your disciple and love the things you love while hating the things you hate. Father, I declare today, that my meat also is to do Your work and to finish it. I will do Your will Father, Help me to do Your will always. Give me the heart of a servant, to serve You with all my heart and to be spend and be spent for You and Your house. Father, teach me obedience that I will loose the ability to do absolutely anything, but what you will that I do in Jesus name. Amen.

title.rendered: 191 – If any man would be my disciple II

content.rendered:
Then said Jesus unto his disciples, If any man will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross, and follow me. [25] For whosoever will save his life shall lose it: and whosoever will lose his life for my sake shall find it.

MATTHEW 16:24-25 KJV

For a person to be a disciple of a man or a cause, he would need to be a diligent observer of the one he follows. Therefore the scripture says in Mark 3:13-14 that He (Jesus) went up on the mountain and summoned those whom He Himself wanted, and they came to Him. And He appointed twelve, so that they would be with Him and that He could send them out to preach. A disciple observes the discipline of the one he follows and does as he sees. Jesus’ disciples saw Him preach and they did the same, but first, they remained with Him. Yesterday, we mentioned a key to consecration, which is our response to the call to follow Jesus: Self-denial.

Jesus lived out a life of self-denial and surrender to God and said to his disciples that they do the same, John 5:30. Another key to consecration or appropriate response to our call is to be a disciple in devotion, praise, and worship to God. Jesus lived and breathed prayer. He prayed when he was being baptized, Luke 3:21-22, being transfigured, Luke 9:28-29, and even before He was killed, Mark 13:32-42, this was how He had the strength to go to the cross. He prayed hours and hours while having one of the busiest schedules a person can have. He would pray all night and minister all day, Luke 5:15-16, Matthew 14:23, Mark 1:35. His busy schedule was never an excuse not to pray, this was how He always knew the will of the Father.

We cannot expect to be as effective as Jesus was without spending hours in prayer. Hebrews 4:16 tells us that we are to come boldly, confidently, with assurance to receive at his throne. If we are to become what God wants us to be in Christ Jesus, we must be in communion with Him. We are already referred to as a house of prayer, Isaiah 56:7. We have the Spirit that enabled Jesus to pray within us and so we can pray as He did.

Another discipline is Studying the Word of God. Paul said to Timothy, study to show yourself approved, 2 Timothy 2:15. Jesus was obviously a student of the Word. Luke 4:16 says And He came to Nazareth, where He had been brought up; and as was His custom, He entered the synagogue on the Sabbath, and stood up to read. He knew the Word and had meditated on it. It was His custom to read the scriptures. This was how he could go through the temptation in Matthew 4:1-11. This was how he could fulfill that which was written of Him in the Scripture. To know God’s will for our lives and the church, we must relate with Him through His Word which is the blueprint. The primary way God speaks to us is through His Word and a disciple must be conversant with the Word of God.

The beauty of being a disciple of Jesus is that the same Spirit He had, we have in us. All the works He did, we can and will do, and more as we observe and follow His discipline because His Spirit lives and also dwells in us, John 14:12. 

Prayer for today: Lord Jesus, thank you for showing me a clear example of what I can be if I choose to be your disciple. Father, help me to stay with You and learn of You. If my world will ever see Jesus through me, I need to learn your discipline and be diligent to observe and do. Lord help me to be diligent and not hasty. Let me pray like You did and study Your word as diligently as You did. I receive Your grace today to pray as You did, that I may also fulfil that which is written of me in the volume of the books, to do Your will in Jesus name. Amen.

title.rendered: 190 – If any man would be my disciple

content.rendered:
Then said Jesus unto his disciples, If any man will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross, and follow me. [25] For whosoever will save his life shall lose it: and whosoever will lose his life for my sake shall find it.

Matthew 16:24-25 KJV

When a person enlists in the army, there are certain physical, aptitude and moral standards that they must meet for each military base. A person enlisting for the army will not walk into the base with multiple tongue and face piercings. They also will pay attention to what they eat during the days leading to their assessment as well as during their time in the military if they are to survive in the army. 2 Timothy 2:4 says, “No man that warreth entangleth himself with the affairs of this life; that he may please him who hath chosen him to be a soldier”. Consecration is necessary for us to be able to attain to the fulness of life and it is our response to the God’s call.

Titus 2:11-13 tells us that the grace of God brings salvation to us and it also teaches us how to progress in our walk with God towards the fulness of Christ which grace will bring us into. This progression includes a cost, which is denying ungodliness and worldly lust, while living soberly and righteously in this present world. In Matthew 16:24-25, Jesus also listed the cost or discipline for all who would enlist in His army as His disciples. Note that this is a choice for the individual, hence Jesus said “If any man will follow me”. It is not a must that a man enter into the fullness of all God has for him and indeed, many would choose not to. However, a life of consecration is required of us as a response if we are to grow into His fulness. How do we practically live a life of consecration to prove we want to go all the way to be like Him?

This meditation explains seven aspects of living a consecrated life, one of which is Self denial. This speaks of denial of the world and its lusts. 1 John 2:15-17 tells us to draw away from the world and calls us to separate ourselves from anything that will hold us back from moving on in this race.The world here is not the physical earth we live in. In John 17:15, Jesus prayed that we should not be taken from the world, but be shielded from the evil one. The world is the anti-god system governed by the devil, who is its god. It is characterized by the lust of the flesh, the lust of the eyes and the pride of life. Sin that was in us was destroyed on the cross, therefore the lust of the flesh, lust of the eyes and pride of life in the world is not in us, Galatians 5:24. This does not however, remove us from temptations and the tendency to act like those in the world out of ignorance. We live in this world, but we are from a world to come, wherein dwells righteousness, peace and Joy, Romans 14:17.

A believer who is still worldly, even though he is saved, hasn’t seen the kingdom of God. The moment a person understands the beauties in the Kingdom of God, his natural response is to enlist in this Kingdom and give up anything that will make him fall short of it. This includes certain legitimate things that are not sin in themselves but could still cause stumbling blocks or weights that slow down our pace (1Corinthians 6:12). A person who has his eyes on the Kingdom wants to please God always in His choices, time, relationships and in every area of his life. He becomes a yes man to God. God has chosen us and called us near to Him, and what He requires of us is to respond to him and do that which will please Him. Beloved, what thing is so precious to you, that you cannot lay down for the Kingdom? If there is such a thing, you have not seen the coming Kingdom. Pray that your eyes be open to see the God who you confess to love!

Prayer for today: Lord Jesus, thank you for your call on my life. Father I pray that You may give unto me the spirit of wisdom and revelation in the knowledge of You: The eyes of my understanding being enlightened; that I may know what is the hope of Your calling, and what the riches of the glory of Your inheritance in the saints. Father, let the Kingdom be instilled in my heart and let my eyes be open to see the God, I confess to love in Jesus name. Amen

And if ye offer a sacrifice of peace offerings unto the LORD, ye shall offer it at your own will.

Leviticus 19:5 KJV

In the old covenant, the priests and the people had five offerings they could offer to the Lord, two of which were compulsory: the sin offering and the whole burnt offering. However, the peace offering was an offering given at will. It is a sign of friendship. The one who offered this was moving beyond the requirements for simply being a part of God’s congregation. He was showing a deeper commitment. The fact that it was an offering at will however, did not mean that God did not have specific instructions for this. It had to be pure and without blemish. God gave instruction for this offering in Leviticus 3:1-17 and Leviticus 7:11-21. For this offering the main ingredients are the fats and the kidneys. They were to be taken out and burnt on the altar as an offering made by fire unto God.

What does it mean to offer our fat and kidney to the Lord? We first of all need to know their function in the body. Fat acts as the body’s energy reservoir. It is a storage for excess food, which can be used later to produce energy. This fat is usually stored in areas of the body that makes a person look more attractive, especially in females. Fat also helps to absorb and store certain key vitamins: A, D, E, K, all of which are essential to proper functioning of the body. It is also one of the main structural components that make up the brain, it helps to maintain body temperature, and is also stored as a layer under the skin. It helps to protect the vital organs of the body from shock due to sudden movement or hard impact. Fat is also responsible for making hormones which put one in a ‘love mood’.

The Kidney on the other hand, is generally understood among the Hebrews as the metaphorical seat of emotions, and figuratively, the mind. The interpretation of the original Greek word “kilyah” shows this. Knowing this, we see how the peace offering is a full on commitment. Offering the peace offering means that we give Him our energy [serve Him with our strength], all the things that make us feel secured [all the things we feel we can always fall back on if something happens], which may include our money, our skills, and even our time. He wants us to give Him all the things that make us attractive or admirable, which may include our talents and more. He also wants our virtues [our vitamins: the things that make us function as the people we are] and our mind [our understanding and intellect]. That is, God wants us to use them for Him [to think on Him and His Word, and to communicate Him and His gospel to all around us]. He also wants our emotions and our desires. He wants us to have deep feelings for Him and tenderly desire Him above all else.

The man Abraham was a man who gave this peace offering regularly to the Lord. He gave up everything, comfort, inheritances of his fathers house and even the son of his love and was called a Friend of God. The beauty of being a friend is that the friend of God knows what God is doing and is brought into a place where he can speak with God face to face. Their say in a matter counts, like in the case of Abraham and Sodom, Genesis 18:17-33. Looking throughout the new covenant, we see that while the basic requirement to being saved is to believe the gospel, John 3:16, Jesus told a rich man who asked, that if he would be an inheritor of the Kingdom, he must give up everything and follow Jesus as His disciple, Mark 10:17-31. This was a commitment. One who refused this level of commitment, will have their sins forgiven and escape the wrath of God, but will gnash their teeth when they see their mates in glory and they, shut out from these blessings. For this reason Paul suffered the loss of all things, Philippians 3:7-10. The Lord Himself gives His strength that we may make peace with Him as Isaiah 27:5-6 says. For all who make peace with Him, He causes a blossoming in their lives, that they may be full of beautiful fruits for all to see and enjoy. Beloved, it is a choice to make, but all who will partake of the fullness of God must give all!

Prayer for today: Father, I thank you for Your word and Your commitment to me. Father, today, I decide to love You with all my heart, soul, strength and mind. I want to be a Your friend Lord, I take hold of Your strength and make peace with You. Father, help me to do Your will always, in Jesus name. Amen. 

{You are making a commitment to God, speak openly and freely to God to express your desire and commitment. He hears you}

Beloved, when I gave all diligence to write unto you of the common salvation, it was needful for me to write unto you, and exhort you that ye should earnestly contend for the faith which was once delivered unto the saints.

Jude 1:3 KJV

In the tech world, when a developer makes additions to the code for an application, they deploy them in versions, so that if there was anything wrong with the newer code, they can always return to the last code that functioned properly. In Jude’s statement in the above verse, he implied that, as at the time he wrote this letter to the church, the common christian faith which was initially given to the apostles of the lamb had gone through various edits and had changed for the worse. There was introduction of ungodliness and extras, with people turning the grace of God into lasciviousness.

In Jude 1:5, Jude made reference to the departure of the Israelites from Egypt and Lot from sodom. Why? First these were written for our examples and were a warning to us. Also, the art of contending for our faith can also be likened to Israel’s departure from Egypt and Lot’s departure from Sodom. This alternated version of the faith has materialized into what can be referred to as Egypt. Revelations 12 and 17 speaks of two women, both were brides, although one had become a whore. In Revelations 18:4, a remarkable statement was made to the bride, or a set of people in that bride — Come out of her, My people.

How did God’s people get inside this woman and who is this woman? Jeremiah 3 gives us a hint. God was in a covenant relationship with Israel. His covenant was so intimate, that it could be referred to as marriage. Isaiah also cried out in Isaiah 1:21, how did this faithful city become a whore? Jeremiah said Israel had a whore’s forehead and had committed adultery with sticks and stones. This just meant, they had their mind set on worshipping idols and did worship idols, whereas, God was their God and husband. Hence, God called them a whore. In our case, the church is the bride of Christ. Therefore, when the church begins to go in the error and greed of Baalam, Cain, esteeming men in their hearts as a thing to be worshipped, etc as Jude 1 says, they are adding updates to the true version and are committing adultery.

The whore in Revelations 17 is also called Babylon and Sodom and Egypt, Revelation 11:8. Why? Babylon was an empire that would conquer nations and absorb their gods into themselves. This just symbolizes the infiltration of Jerusalem, where you could find sacred items from Solomons in the same temple as foreign gods, Daniel 5:1-6. In Sodom, while being evil, you Lot remained there, vexing his righteous soul, 2 Peter 2:7-8. Egypt was once a golden cup in God’s hand. God used Egypt to save the world from death by famine and preserve His people, yet she became an enemy of God. God had to send Moses to deliver His people from her and destroy Egypt.

The call to contend for the faith and depart from alterations from the true faith is like the call for Lot to leave Sodom and Israel to leave Egypt, not just the place but the practices and Idolatry that makes Egypt, Babylon and Sodom. When a christian concert, starts singing worldly songs in order to excite the people and then moves over to worshipping God, this is Egypt and Babylon. When a person serves God and Mammon, this is Egypt and Babylon. When men are exalted and reverenced as Idols or God’s representative above their brethren, this is Babylon and Egypt.

Beloved, search inward and look through the version of the faith you have as an individual. How aligned are you to the original faith committed to us in the bible? Look at your environment and associations, are you in Babylon or Sodom, vexing your righteous soul like Lot? This call is time sensitive. There is a judgment pronounced over Babylon, Egypt and Sodom as seen in Revelations 17 and 18. Those who heed now, will be used like Moses to deliver Israel, like the Abraham to deliver Lot, like Zerubbabel who exited Babylon to rebuild the true temple of God. 

Prayer for today: Heavenly Father, thank you for Your word to me today. Lord examine my heart and see where I may have strayed from the true faith that You handed down to Your disciples. Show me any way I may have fallen short Lord, any infiltrations, any Babylon within and heal my backsliding. I choose to return to the bible and to live by Your word. Teach me Your ways that I may walk in Your truth. Lord If I am also like Lot, in a place that vexes my righteous soul, show me what I need to do and how do deliver my soul, that I will not partake of her sins and judgement in Jesus name, Amen.

content.rendered:
But be not ye called Rabbi: for one is your Master, even Christ; and all ye are brethren. [9] And call no man your father upon the earth: for one is your Father, which is in heaven. [10] Neither be ye called masters: for one is your Master, even Christ. [11] But he that is greatest among you shall be your servant

Matthew 23:8-11 KJV

In the above scripture, Jesus was training his disciples and showing them what His ideals were for His church in which they will be pillars. This, however, does not seem to be the case in our current day with men and women taking on ministry gifts as titles. Ephesians 4:11-12 says


And he gave some, apostles; and some, prophets; and some, evangelists; and some, pastors and teachers; [12] For the perfecting of the saints, for the work of the ministry, for the edifying of the body of Christ:

This implies that there are ministry gifts in the body of Christ. Acts 13:1-2 also identified these ministry gifts in churches. However, where do we draw the line between identifying these gifts and obeying the command of Jesus in Matthew 23:8-11?

In our world, when a person becomes a prime minister or a president, he needs to form a cabinet for himself. Even before he assigns persons to the cabinet, the roles already exist. These roles do not become a part of the assigned individual’s names. It is an office and a task which they are assigned to do. In order to understand Jesus’s command in Matthew 23:8-11, we need to explore His heart behind calling people to serve in His Kingdom

Mark 3:14 says:
And he (Jesus) ordained twelve, that they should be with him, and that he might send them forth to preach,

Jesus set the clear expectation for all who would be relevant in his house. First, they were to be with Him. Next, they were to go as messengers to do the task He sends them and then they were to return to be with Him. We need to clearly understand that God is sufficient in Himself to do all the work. He has the power to be everywhere at any time without any loss of power or ability. However, it is His pleasure to use men. The reason why he selects a cabinet is primarily to be with Him. Their major calling is to be His companion and friend. Even greater, Jesus called us brothers, Hebrews 2:11-18. This is the greatest name a person can have in the church of Christ.

So why did Jesus frown against titles? This is because titles create a hierarchy in the body of Christ. This error was caused by Constantine when he felt the need to merge the church and the state and tried to mirror the hierarchy of the state into the church of God. God never intended to have children and grandchildren, so when a person exalts himself by adding titles, he is subconsciously elevating himself above the realm of being a brother.

Ephesians 4:11-12 shows that Jesus himself assigns offices to men. This means His intent is that in every local assembly, there will be an expression of an apostle, prophets, teachers, evangelists, and shepherds. These may be in a formative state, but they are there. There are also bishops who serve or oversee a particular function in the church and there are deacons who serve as Paul always assigned in churches, Acts 14:23. Yet, Jesus can send someone to be a teacher in one assembly and as a shepherd in another, because the work is His and He knows what each congregation needs. However, for a person to add that as a title to their name causes unnecessary elevations and pressure. A person calling himself a prophet may put himself under the pressure to prophesy whether led by the Lord or not, just to meet the expectations of those who call him by that name. Hence Jesus said, you are all to be called brethren (brothers and sisters).

The body of Christ is a living organism and it is able to recognize the function of each part. The hand knows and understands the function of the eye. Most importantly, the Lord knows and recognizes each part and function. There is no need for an announcement because a man’s gifts make room for him, Proverbs 18:16. Yet Jesus, foreseeing the potential harm title-giving has in the church warned against it. This is also what is called the Nicolaitan spirit (Conquerors over the laity), Revelations 2:6, 14-15. This was what caused the downfall of mighty revivals like Azusa street and also the beginning of the dark ages after the death of the apostles.

Beloved, there is beauty in simplicity as the Lord ordained it. The Lord had always loved to dwell among those that are outcasts and not the juggernauts. Let us learn of Him, for He is meek and lowly in heart, Mark 11:29. There we will find rests for our souls. 

Prayer for today: Father, when I consider the fact that the Son of God, who holds all things by the Word of His power. The one who made the heavens and the earth would call me a brother, I am filled with deep awe and admiration for Your person. Help me today to learn of You. You are an embodiment of beauty, meekness and lowliness. I want to be like you Lord Jesus and then I will find rest for my soul. Help me to be lowly in heart and embrace meekness as a chief Joy in Jesus name. Amen.

title.rendered: 186 – The flesh and the Spirit – two rival forces II

content.rendered:
For they that are after the flesh do mind the things of the flesh; but they that are after the Spirit the things of the Spirit. [6] For to be carnally minded is death; but to be spiritually minded is life and peace. [7] Because the carnal mind is enmity against God: for it is not subject to the law of God, neither indeed can be. [8] So then they that are in the flesh cannot please God. [9] But ye are not in the flesh, but in the Spirit, if so be that the Spirit of God dwell in you. Now if any man have not the Spirit of Christ, he is none of his.

ROMANS 8:5-9 KJV

Throughout scriptures, we see a recurring theme of a battle between the two from the same source, one being righteous and the other a rival. In the beginning, in the midst of the garden of the Lord, there was the tree of knowledge of good and evil and there was also the tree of life. From Adam came Abel, but there was also Cain. Cain persecuted Abel, Genesis 4. There was Isaac and Ishmael, the seed of promise and the seed of the bond woman, Ishmael persecuted Isaac and his children still do till this day, Genesis 21:10. From Isaac came Jacob and Esau and through out the history of these two, we see the persecution of Jacob by Esau and all of his Children, the amalekites, etc. We also see Saul and David, both anointed King, but one rejected by God and another a King in God’s eyes, 1 Samuel 16:1. There is Jerusalem above which is who we are and the Jerusalem beneath, Galatians 4:22-31. All these typify the warfare that the righteous go through. Esau’s name was changed to Edom, which means Earthy and Jacob was changed to Israel, who is a prince with God.

In essence, right from the beginning, the righteous has been faced with a war to obtain the promise of God and this war has been with an immediate rival. For us, the war is between our old nature and our new nature. The two hate each other as Romans 8 says. Ever wonder why you could watch a show till midnight, but sleep the moment you pick up a bible? Paul ranted about this internal battle in Romans 7, saying “For I know that in me (that is, in my flesh,) dwelleth no good thing: for to will is present with me; but how to perform that which is good I find not. [19] For the good that I would I do not: but the evil which I would not, that I do.” – Romans 7:18-19 KJV. We have a promise to receive the Kingdom of God. Yet, flesh and blood cannot inherit this Kingdom, 1 Corinthians 15:50.

How then do we win this battle? Why the flesh has been destroyed by the death of Christ, we are in this world, ruled by the same one who dwelt in the flesh, Sin. The bible says that the physical things show the clearly the things of the Spirit, Romans 1:20, and so we will pick up an illustration for ease of understanding. We can liken the law of sin and death to physical gravity. We said yesterday, that the man in Christ is a like a satellite ship designed to dwell in outer space, outside the realm of gravity. The bible says the righteous will shine like the Sun, Matthew 13:43, this is our destination, to be as the Sun of righteousness, giving life and light to the earth. However, there are layers that a physical rocket ship must go through to get to the sun.

It begins from the earth or ground, which is where gravity pulls all objects towards. There is the troposphere, where airplanes and birds fly, right before the Ozone layer. Then there is the Stratosphere then the Mesosphere where the Karma layer begins ‘Outer space’. Prior to the karma layer, the heat of the sun is not really felt and it can be as cold as -86.5C. Next there is Thermosphere. Here there is a drastic switch in temperature and this satellite begins to experience the sun, getting as hot as 1200C. This also begins the ionosphere which also contains the Exosphere where most space ships float. Finally the Magnetosphere, where the Sun is.

The point of this was not to give a geography crash course. With each layer this satellite gets to, the pull of gravity is less and less intense, up until the exosphere, where gravity disappears. For a rocket to bypass gravity, it needs what is called Escape velocity. As it goes higher, the velocity remains until it gets outside the reach of gravity, where it can float freely in space. We can liken escape to the law of the Spirit of life in Christ Jesus. It is a different law that that of sin and death, which confines man to the earth. This law is from the Spirit of life in the Word of God. The bible says the word of God can convert the soul, Psalm 19:6. Paul also says when we renew our minds by the Word of God, we are transfigured, Romans 12:1, 2 Corinthians 3:18. What it does is remove condemnation and guilt, while giving you a right standing with God that allows you to approach God without fear or guilt. There is a reason Satan is called the accuser of the brethren in Revelations 12:10-12. His accusation pulls people away from God towards the earth. This was how he destroyed Judas Iscariot and many others. This is also the biggest force we are to overcome. A person who has been told a million times that he would never be righteous, begins to believe it and will never be righteous.

However, beloved, you can be and are already righteous. There is no condemnation for you, who lives in Christ Jesus, walking not after the flesh but after the Spirit, Romans 8:1. You are not in the flesh! (Romans 8:9) Paul says, Know ye not that your old man was crucified, Romans 6:3-6. Jesus said “Be of good cheer, I have overcome the world”, John 16:33. All you need to advance in the heavens has been given to you, 2 Peter 1:2-3. As a wise saint once said ‘read your bible and pray everyday if you want to grow’. The point of this message is you need to understand and know that you are not in the flesh. You also need to know there will be resistance to obtain the promise of being like Christ, but you need to decide not to give up. You most likely will not immediately feel the impact of your bible study or prayer, just like the rocket ship aiming to get to the sun. At first, it’s cold and one may think, with all the resistance, it may not even be approaching the sun. Yet as you go deeper, you will find out that God is a rewarder of those who diligently seek. Mount on eagles wings as you wait on the Lord, beloved and soar in the Spirit. 

Prayer for today: Father, I thank you because in you is all I need for life and godliness. I also thank you because you have given unto me the law of the Spirit of life in Christ Jesus. I have the mind of Christ! Father, teach me the art of waiting on you, that I may always have the wings of an eagle to soar high in the Spirit. Help me to be a diligent seeker of God, in prayer and by studying the Word of God. I know you reward those that seek you. It is my destiny to shine like My Father in heaven, the Sun of Righteousness in Jesus name Amen.

title.rendered: 185- The flesh and the Spirit – two rival forces

content.rendered:
For they that are after the flesh do mind the things of the flesh; but they that are after the Spirit the things of the Spirit. [6] For to be carnally minded is death; but to be spiritually minded is life and peace. [7] Because the carnal mind is enmity against God: for it is not subject to the law of God, neither indeed can be. [8] So then they that are in the flesh cannot please God. [9] But ye are not in the flesh, but in the Spirit, if so be that the Spirit of God dwell in you. Now if any man have not the Spirit of Christ, he is none of his.

Romans 8:5-9 KJV

God is a Spirit. Therefore everyone who is born of God is Spirit. In John 3:5-6 Jesus answered, Verily, verily, I say unto thee, Except a man be born of water and of the Spirit, he cannot enter into the kingdom of God. [6] That which is born of the flesh is flesh; and that which is born of the Spirit is spirit. All who are born again of the Spirit are simply having an human experience and possess a soul whose salvation is the end of our faith as 1 Peter 1:9 says. Yet prior to this, in Genesis 3, Adam who had been called a son of God took on a different nature when he fell from his estate previously assigned to him by God. When man died, he became flesh and subject to death.

What is the flesh? Contrary to popular opinion, the flesh isn’t simply the human body, since the bible says our bodies are the temple of the Holy Spirit, 1 Corinthians 6:19. It is that in man which is at enmity with God as Romans 8 explains. It is the earthy nature that is apart from Divine Influence. It is impossible to please God in the flesh because there is no meeting point between the Spirit and the flesh. This flesh and the Spirit are in two different realms. Just like everything on earth obeys the laws of gravity and everything outer space floats, not being subject to gravity, the flesh serves the law of sin and death, while the Spirit serves the law of the Spirit of Life in Christ Jesus. Just like the bible refers to this world, not as the physical earth, but a system controlled by the devil who is called its prince, the flesh is controlled by the devil, the person of sin himself, John 14:30, 1 John 2:16.

The flesh manifests itself in various works: Anger, malice, envy, wickedness are all expressions of the nature of the flesh, Galatians 5:19-21. One who is ruled by the flesh cannot really help these expressions. Walking contrary will be like asking a fish to swim out of water. The good news however, is that this is why the Son of God was made manifest, to destroy the works of the devil, the person of Sin, 1 John 3:8. Jesus embodied sin and took on the flesh nature for the purpose of nailing it to the cross. When he died, the veil was broken, which veil was the flesh (that which separated us from God), Ephesians 2:15,Hebrews 10:19-20, Hebrews 2:14-18. They that are Christs have crucified the flesh. Sin no longer has dominion over a believer.

If this is the case, why then do believers still walk in anger, malice, etc? Good question! It is no longer the norm for believers to walk in sin. Recall we spoke about world, which is the anti God system ruled by the devil. We have been delivered from the sin within, but we are in this world which stinks of sin. The man in Christ is a like a satellite ship designed to dwell in outer space, outside the realm of gravity. He was created in the heavens to rule in the heavens. However, to escape the pull of gravity isn’t for the faint hearted. A rocket ship, in the physical would need to pass through to a seventh layers get to get outer space and remain there, escaping gravity. We will consider this in more details in a subsequent meditation. However, know this beloved, that they that are Christ’s have crucified the flesh and all of its lust, Galatians 5:24. You can live above sin always. This was why Jesus died, that you may be free and free indeed. 

Prayer for today: Father I thank you, because though I was born into sin, being ruled by my fleshly desires and nature, You came to give me a choice. You set me free and so I am no longer a slave. I actually can choose not to sin, Hallelujah! Father, teach me how to live above sin, to live by the law of the Spirit of life in Christ Jesus. I am not in the flesh! I am dead to the flesh and alive to God and sin no longer has dominion over me. Teach me everyday to choose life Lord, that I may live in Jesus name. Amen.

excerpt.rendered: God is a Spirit. Therefore everyone who is born of God is Spirit. In John 3:5-6 Jesus answered, Verily, verily, I say unto thee, Except a man be born of water and of the Spirit, he cannot enter into the kingdom of God. [6] That which is born of the flesh is flesh; and that which is born of the Spirit is spirit. All who are born again of the Spirit are simply having an human experience and possess a soul whose salvation is the end of our faith as 1 Peter 1:9 says. Yet prior to this, in Genesis 3, Adam who had been called a son of God took on a different nature when he fell from his estate previously assigned to him by God. When man died, he became flesh and subject to death. The flesh and the Spirit are always at war with each other.

content.rendered:
Thou art worthy, O Lord, to receive glory and honour and power: for thou hast created all things, and for thy pleasure they are and were created.

Revelation 4:10 kjv

God is the one and only true God, a great King. He made all things for to reveal His splendour and give Him glory, including man. This is the whole duty of man. The book of Esther captured a living parable of a great king and his subjects in the Persian empire. This King in the third year after receiving the Kingdom decided to throw a feast for all people. In this feast, He decided to showcase His most valued treasure, which was his wife, Vashti (meaning beautiful). However, due to rebellion and pride, she did not come. This greatly displeased the king. He was furious and stripped her off all authority and the estate he had given her. After his anger had subsided, his servants said to Him,

Esther 2:2,4 KJV
Then said the king’s servants that ministered unto him, Let there be fair young virgins sought for the king: [4] And let the maiden which pleaseth the king be queen instead of Vashti. And the thing pleased the king; and he did so.

The King only does what pleases Him. And so in Esther 2, the search for the new queen began with a few criteria: She must be a virgin, she was beautiful and she pleased the king. In terms of the beauty, the King provided for all that would make her beautiful. There were six months of myrrh and six months of sweet spices to prepare all the virgins. However, only one will become the queen and the others will need to be worked on again in the house of the concubines and may or may never see the king again. Regardless, they would all be subject to the queen. Esther became the queen; she stood out in her choices. The major difference between her and Vashti was not in beauty or that she was a virgin, but that Esther displayed meekness where Vashti displayed pride. Where every virgin would choose what they wanted to go to the king, Esther, deferred her choice to the King’s chamberlains who were instructed to prepare her to meet the king. She never did anything by her own wisdom or counsel.

These things were written for us, upon whom the end of the world is come, 1 Corinthians 10:11. The bible says that without faith, it is impossible to please God, Hebrews 11:6. In our case there was a bride before us this bride was the old covenant. Not that the covenant was bad, but Hebrews 8:7-8 Said God had a fault with those who served under the law. These make up the Jerusalem below and the observers of the law, Galatians 4:22-31. What will make a believer to fall out of grace in this time is not necessarily what they do, but over dependence on the law to get righteousness. Righteousness is a right standing with God and a right to rule). Under the old covenant, righteousness is a reward. However, in the new covenant, the righteousness is a gift, Romans 5:17. If we take this as a reward, it is no longer reckoned to us as a gift. The fault with the Old covenant was that the they depended on their works. Our King has already provided all that we need to please Him and part of this is faith. It is a fruit of the Spirit as Galatians 5:22-24. What does this mean? It means that as we interact with Word of God and His Spirit (Which are a type of the Chamberlains), faith is being formed in us.

Whose faith? Paul said in: Galatians 2:20-21 KJV
I am crucified with Christ: nevertheless I live; yet not I, but Christ liveth in me: and the life which I now live in the flesh I live by the faith of the Son of God, who loved me, and gave himself for me. [21] I do not frustrate the grace of God: for if righteousness come by the law, then Christ is dead in vain.

It is the faith of the Son of God, not our faith, that made Jesus pleasing to God at all times. It is also by His faith that we were accepted in Him, the beloved. This does not disregard works, because faith without works is dead. The proof that we believe, is that we do the works He did. The work of God is to believe and obey, John 6:29. Faith is not name it and claim it. Contrary to popular opinion, confessing is not receiving; Obedience is receiving. The work is the work of faith expressed by an obedience to God’s command. 

We are in a selection process for all those who will become the bride of Christ and reign with Him forever. Yet, the command has gone out, that it is the virgin hearted ( single eyed and devoted) believers, being beautified with the beauty of Christ who please the King of Kings, by displaying the faith of God received via their interaction with the Word and Spirit, that will be queen and reign forever. 

Prayer for today: Thou art Worthy o Lord to receive Glory, Honour and power, For I was created for your pleasure. For your pleasure I exist and will live continually. Father, may I please You always, living by the faith of the Son of God. All that are Christ's have crucified the flesh, which was at constant enmity with You. I choose to live today and always by the faith of Jesus who loved me and gave Himself for me. Help me always to please You in Jesus name. Amen

title.rendered: 183 – The Anatomy of the renewed mind VII

content.rendered:
I beseech you therefore, brethren, by the mercies of God, that ye present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable unto God, which is your reasonable service. [2] And be not conformed to this world: but be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind, that ye may prove what is that good, and acceptable, and perfect, will of God.

ROMANS 12:1-2 KJV

We’ve been on a series considering the renewed mind and the unrenewed mind. Our case study has been Abraham and Lot, who typify believers with a renewed mind and unrenewed mind respectively. Considering Genesis 18 and 19, we concluded yesterday’s meditation by saying that God’s messages to the believer with the renewed mind are always that of revelation and responsibility which brings Joy, while His message to the believer with an unrenewed mind is always that of repentance and rescue, which brings Sorrow.

In Genesis 18, Abraham was rewarded with a unique ability to intercede for a whole nation because God could trust him. It was by this interceeding that he saved his nephew Lot. God called Abraham, His friend. As mentioned in a previous meditation, God is at home in the heart of a believer with a renewed mind, because his heart is full of faith towards God. Abraham had learned to see things from an eternal perspective. Unlike Lot who had sat at the gates of Sodom vexing his righteous soul with evil associations as 2 Peter 2:8 says, Abraham won favor with God and could bargain with God as a friend would.

In Genesis 19:4-11, the angels had just departed from Abraham and came to Sodom to observe the city and see if it was worth saving. Upon getting there, the men of the city tried to rape these angels, but Lot, still thinking carnally, offered his virgin daughters instead. You cannot erase evil by practicing lesser evil or with worldly goodness. Moving on, the men of the city refused and moved to attack him. Lot probably had no idea that his being at the gates of Sodom yielded no fruits for God until this day when the men of the city absolutely despised him. In Genesis 19:9-10 – Lot had no influence with the men of Sodom. In Genesis 19:14-16, Lot had no influence over his sons-in-law, wife, and daughters. You yield zero influence for God when you play by the rules of the world or use human strength and goodness.

You can’t influence people with heaven’s agenda if your mind doesn’t glisten like heaven. Miracles done in the space of carnal Christians are solely for the purpose of entertainment. (The sign of blindness didn’t awaken Lot’s son’s in-law, or convict Lot’s wife, it didn’t correct Lot’s daughters or strengthen Lot’s hands). In the case of Abraham however, we can see that the renewed mind uses the love of God as a valid reason to change the world. The renewed mind is so enclosed in the love of God that the entire being is expanded to contain the full expression of the fullness of God, Colossians 3:17-19. With the renewed mind the righteous increase in territory and influence as the years go by, with the unrenewed mind, the righteous decrease in territory and influence as the years go by.

In conclusion, the renewing of the mind is the work of the Holy Spirit. To the measure we yield to Him, we are transformed from glory to glory. To renew our minds, we need to read our bibles, study and meditate on it and mix it with Prayer. Open yourself to receive from the body of Christ through prophetic messages, books, and spiritual gatherings. Finally, promptly obey and practice the Word of God. Allow it to form your convictions and conversations. You must have a culture of unapologetically saying what God says – Your words must be the words of God for your days to be as the days of heaven on the earth.

Our world needs to see Jesus and it will, through men and women who have the mind of Christ! Beloved, you have the mind of Christ! Allow it have an expression in you!

Prayer for today: Heavenly Father, thank you for the cross where my flesh and carnal mind were crucified in Christ. Your Word says that I have the mind of Christ and that all who are in Christ have crucified the flesh with all of its lust. I confess that this is my reality. Help me to be diligent in studying the Word and obeying your command. I know that as I gaze at Your beauty through Your Word, I will be transformed into Your likeness. Amen.

title.rendered: 182 – The Anatomy of the Renewed mind VI

content.rendered:
I beseech you therefore, brethren, by the mercies of God, that ye present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable unto God, which is your reasonable service. [2] And be not conformed to this world: but be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind, that ye may prove what is that good, and acceptable, and perfect, will of God.

ROMANS 12:1-2 KJV

Our recent meditations have been on the characteristics of a believer possessing a renewed mind versus an unrenewed mind, exploring the differences in lifestyle, motivation, and the ultimate consequence of possessing either. Abraham’s attitude towards God and His angels, when compared to Lot’s, shows differences that are worthy of note when comparing a renewed and an unrenewed mind. In Genesis 18 and 19, both Abraham and Lot encountered messengers of the Lord. Yesterday, we mentioned that God is at home with a believer with a renewed mind due to the presence of faith in them. However, the unrenewed mind is at enmity with God, Romans 8:7. God was quick to accept Abraham’s hospitable advances but rejected Lot’s.

The renewed mind – revealed in service to God.

Abraham: So Abraham hurried into the tent to Sarah. “Quick,” he said, “get three seahs of fine flour and knead it and bake some bread.” (7) Then he ran to the herd and selected a choice, tender calf, and gave it to a servant, who hurried to prepare it. (8) He then brought some curds and milk and the calf that had been prepared and set these before them. While they ate, he stood near them under a tree. Genesis 18:6-8 (NIV).

Lot: My lords,” he said, “please turn aside to your servant’s house. You can wash your feet and spend the night and then go on your way early in the morning.” “No,” they answered, “we will spend the night in the square.” (3) But he insisted so strongly that they did go with him and entered his house. He prepared a meal for them, baking bread without yeast, and they ate. Genesis 19:2-3(NIV)

One of the vital ways you can recognize a renewed mind is not just in service to God but in the attitude of their service to God. Throughout the narrative we can see several words used to convey Abraham’s service to God: he hurried, he hurried again, he ran, he said ‘quick’! Lot did not show such an attitude. He had a rather sluggish approach. It would be the attitude of Lot to arrive at his quiet times with God or the gathering of the saints sluggishly. Abraham didn’t just hurry – he inspired that attitude in his household. This culture of ministering to the Lord is contagious! Abraham considered curds, milk, a choice, and tender calf for three grown men a morsel of bread! This was his attitude to God’s work. The renewed mind has a culture of urgency – it is swift in purpose in the things of the Spirit.

Genesis 18:9-10 captured God’s further dealings with the renewed mind. God’s messages to the believer with the renewed mind are always that of revelation and responsibility which comes with Joy. Here God revealed to Abraham His intent to make Sarah who was barren, a mother of many nations. God’s message to the believer with the unrenewed mind, however, is always that of repentance and rescue, which comes with sorrow. While the Lord was entrusting Isaac to Abraham, He was rescuing Lot from judgment by fire.

God is not mocked. He is also a faithful rewarder. Whatsoever a man sows, he will reap. The soul of the sluggard desireth, and hath nothing: but the soul of the diligent shall be made fat. Proverbs 13:4. 

Prayer for today: Heavenly Father, thank you for sending Your Word to me today. Lord I have heard Your voice and I choose to awake from any form of spiritual slumber I may have entertained. Father, deliver me from slothfulness and make me diligent in your work. Turn my desires towards you that my soul may delight in the fatness that is in your presence. Let the things of God be my meat and drink and everything else as dung to me. I pray in Jesus' name, Amen.

excerpt.rendered: One of the vital ways you can recognize a renewed mind is not just in service to God but in the attitude of their service to God. Throughout the narrative we can see several words used to convey Abraham’s service to God: he hurried, he hurried again, he ran, he said ‘quick’! Lot did not show such an attitude. He had a rather sluggish approach. It would be the attitude of Lot to arrive at his quiet times with God or the gathering of the saints sluggishly. Abraham didn’t just hurry – he inspired that attitude in his household. This culture of ministering to the Lord is contagious! Abraham considered curds, milk, a choice, and tender calf for three grown men a morsel of bread! This was his attitude to God’s work. The renewed mind has a culture of urgency – it is swift in purpose in the things of the Spirit.

title.rendered: 181 – The Anatomy of the renewed mind V

content.rendered:
Therefore, I urge you, brothers and sisters, in view of God’s mercy, to offer your bodies as a living sacrifice, holy and pleasing to God—this is your true and proper worship. [2] Do not conform to the pattern of this world, but be transformed by the renewing of your mind. Then you will be able to test and approve what God’s will is—his good, pleasing and perfect will.

Romans 12:1-2 NIV

Paul and Peter in Ephesians 6:14 and 1 Peter 1:13 refer to the mind as the loins of the believer because it is the reproductive part of our spiritual life. Nothing comes into this world without the mind testing and approving it. Lot and Abraham typified an un renewed and a renewed mind, respectively in Genesis 13, which has been the focus of our meditation. Yesterday, we said that the renewed mind has a solemn vow to live by the unseen realities of God. The un-renewed mind, however, settles for less as God’s more. All the devil needed to silence Lot in Genesis 13, was the greeneries of Sodom. Lot was spiritually blind and as a result, he was at the mercy of the kings who invaded Sodom in Genesis 14. The unfortunate consequence of having a mind that sees only the things in the earth realm is that whatever affects the world affects the man with the un renewed mind.

Moving on, there was also a major difference in the attitude of Abraham and Lot when entertaining the angels of the Lord in Genesis 18 and 19.

Abraham: The Lord appeared to Abraham near the great trees of Mamre while he was sitting at the entrance to his tent in the heat of the day. Abraham looked up and saw three men standing nearby. When he saw them, he hurried from the entrance of his tent to meet them and bowed low to the ground.  Genesis 18:1-2. NIV

Lot: The two angels arrived at Sodom in the evening, and Lot was sitting in the gateway of the city. When he saw them, he got up to meet them and bowed down with his face to the ground. Genesis 19:1

There are a few things to pick from these scriptures. Abraham was sitting at the entrance of his tent in the heat of the day. He must have been sun gazing. The tent is a place of prayer. The sun of righteousness symbolizes Christ, Malachi 4:2. Abraham must have been in a meditative state and this was why he would immediately notice the angels, but not just notice them he ran to them. We can typify Abraham as a believer who was meditating on Jesus, the Sun of Righteousness. The bible says, we are to let the word of Christ dwell in us richly, Colossians 3:1-2, 16. How? By meditation. Meditation is ‘Hagar’ which means to mutter. We are to mutter the word of Christ to ourselves – “Hagar”. Engage the Spirit of God with the scriptures until your environment takes on the colour of your home from heaven. It’s in meditation, prayer, study of the word and interaction with these spiritual realities that we build our personal history with God.

In the case of Lot, He was at the gates of Sodom in the dark…typifying the believer walking in darkness. He was sitting at the gates, which is where the elders of the land sit. The gate, like in the case of Ruth 4:11, is where important decisions are made. This means Lot was in a place of influence, but had no desire to save the city of sodom when the Angels of the Lord came to him. He did notice the angels coming to him as well, because he was a believer, but his reaction was different. There was no indication of urgency, as was the case of Abraham.

In Genesis 18:3-5, Abraham showed His eagerness to entertain these angels in his Home. Right there, his mindset was to ensure that these angels were taken care of, fed and rested since they had come into his home. The angels accepted Abraham’s invitation. Lot on the other hand also offered hospitality and a place for the angels to sleep and wash their feet. However, the angels declined. This brings us to an important point as we conclude this meditation, God lives in the believer but is only at home with the believer with a renewed mind’s activating faith. The believer with the un renewed mind is in-dwelt by the Spirit but never filled with the Spirit. He contains the Holy Spirit, but is never controlled by the Holy Spirit. He confesses the Lord but doesn’t know the Lord he confesses.

Beloved, spend time gazing at the Sun of Righteousness and in no time, you will begin glistering as the one who has called you to Life and Light. Amen. 

Prayer for today: Heavenly Father, I appreciate you. Father, help me to be a person who delights in Your word. Let it be my meditation day and night. Let psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, continue to rise up from within me to You, all the days of my life, that Christ may dwell and be at home in my heart by faith in Jesus name. Amen

title.rendered: 180 – The Anatomy of the renewed mind IV

content.rendered:
I beseech you therefore, brethren, by the mercies of God, that ye present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable unto God, which is your reasonable service. [2] And be not conformed to this world: but be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind, that ye may prove what is that good, and acceptable, and perfect, will of God.

ROMANS 12:1-2 KJV

The state of mind of a believer determines the quality of life he/ she would have. This is why Peter said in 1 Peter 1:13 to gird up the loins of our mind. Paul also advised in Ephesians 6:14 that our loins be girded with truth. The mind is referred to as the loins because it is the reproductive part of our spiritual life. Nothing comes into this world without the mind testing and approving it. The means of God’s royal entry into the earth is through the brilliance or radiance of the transformed mind. In yesterdays meditation, we identified from the life of Abraham and Lot, the difference between a renewed mind and an un renewed mind. The renewed mind understands the transforming power of an altar or a place of devotion to God. This is where it downloads the wisdom, understanding, counsel, might, knowledge and fear of the Lord from heavens resources. We also mentioned that the renewed mind does everything for gain of love, validating its spiritual exploits – while the un renewed mind does everything for the love of gain, making its spiritual exploits vain and futile, 1 Corinthians 13:1-3.

Another marker of the renewed mind is its solemn vow to live by the unseen realities of God. Having an un renewed mind is a life sentence to live at the level of animal existence. We can only walk by faith when we see by faith. It’s useless to try to walk by faith when you see by sensory perceptions. In Genesis 13:10-18, Abraham and Lot both saw the land before them, however, they made different choices of lands because of their difference in Spiritual understanding. Lot saw green luscious lands and did not realize it was Sodom that would be destroyed. Abraham’s land, while not being physically luscious was the land of promise, flowing with milk and honey. All the devil needed to silence lot was the greenery in sodom. Many destinies have been silenced by choices informed by all that meets the eyes – Ladies marrying because of wealth and six packs. Guys marrying because of physical beauty, ministers of the gospel silenced because of job offers, etc.

If the mind doesn’t draw from heaven, it’ll automatically credit earth as heaven. Lot saw sodom as the “Garden of the Lord”. The un-renewed mind settles for less as God’s more. It approves what is not of God as God and gives it governing influence. Joseph’s heart was on God before he arrived at Egypt and when he arrived at Egypt, Egypt was blessed by him. Daniel’s heart was on God before he arrived at Babylon and when he arrived at Babylon, it was blessed by him. Lot’s heart was on Sodom before he arrived there and when he arrived there, Sodom bankrupted him.

The unfortunate consequence of having a mind that sees only the things in the earth realm is that whatever affects the world affects the man with the unrenewed mind. When people are depressed, they are depressed, when people are addicted, they are addicted, when people live in bondage to the stronghold of mammon, they live in bondage to the stronghold of mammon. When we see a believer continuously carried away in bondage – the first point of concern should be what has dominion over that believer’s mind. In the case of Lot, in Genesis 14:1-17, he was affected by the war that affected Sodom and had to hope on his uncle Abraham for his deliverance. Righteous Lot (a symbol of the one with an un renewed mind) will always be at the mercy of righteous Abraham (a symbol of the one with a renewed mind). Beloved, having a renewed mind is not a choice. It is necessary for all who will overcome in the coming days. 

Prayer for today: Lord Jesus, thank you for sending Your word to me today. Jesus please turn away my eyes from looking at worthless things and restore me in Your ways. May my eyes be set on things above where You are seated in the heavens. May the things of this world become strangely dim in the light of You in Jesus name. Amen.
